chunks: Some of our companions narrated it in mursal form from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Dāwūd ibn Kathīr al-Raqqī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “What is the meaning of the salām upon Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?” So he said: “Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created His Prophet, his وصي, his daughter, his two sons, and all of the Imams, and created their Shiʿah, He took the covenant from them: that they should be patient, urge one another to patience, stand firm, and have taqwa of Allah.”

And He promised them that He would deliver to them the blessed earth and the secure sanctuary, and that He would bring down for them al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, manifest to them the raised roof, grant them relief from their enemy, and the land which Allah will transform into peace, and deliver whatever is in it to them, with no blemish in it.

He said: “There will be no contention there from their enemies, and they shall have therein whatever they love. Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم took the covenant regarding that from all of the Imams and their Shiʿah. The salām upon him is only a reminder of the very covenant itself and a renewal of it before Allah, so that perhaps He, Mighty and Majestic, may hasten it and hasten for you the peace with all that is in it.”

key_terms.السَّقْفَ الْمَرْفُوعَ: the raised roof, mentioned among the unveiled divine realities shown to them
key_terms.السَّلَامِ: the salutation of peace; here, a covenantal invocation upon Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ الْمُبَارَكَةَ: the blessed land promised to them
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ الْمَعْمُورَ: the oft-frequented House, presented here as part of the divine promise
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ الْآمِنَ: the secure sanctuary promised to them
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقَ: the covenant taken by Allah upon the Prophet, the Imams, and their Shiʿah
key_terms.تَذْكِرَةُ: a reminder; here, the salām serves as a reminder of the covenant
key_terms.شِيعَتَهُمْ: their Shiʿah, the followers and loyal adherents of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of saying salām upon Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that sending salām upon Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is tied to a primordial covenant taken from the Prophet, the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, and their Shiʿah. It presents that salām as a remembrance and renewal of that covenant, linked to divine promise, steadfastness, taqwa, and the final granting of peace and security.

en.hubeali: Some of our companions, raising it, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from DAwood Bin Kaseer Al Raqqy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the Meaning of the greetings upon Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, when He<sup>azwj</sup> Created His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> successor<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> daughter, and his<sup>saww</sup> two (grand) sons<sup>asws</sup>, and the entirety of the Imams<sup>asws</sup>, and Created their<sup>asws</sup> Shias, Took the Covenant upon them that they would be patient, and (make others to) observe patience, and that they would fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

And He<sup>azwj</sup> Promised them that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Submit the Blessed earth to them, and the ‘الْحَرَمَ الْآمِنَ’ Just Al-Harrum, and that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Bring down the Oft-Frequented House (Bayt Al-Mamour) to them, and He<sup>azwj</sup> would Manifest the Raised Ceiling to them, and Given them rest/respite from their enemies, and the earth Which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Change for them from the peace and safety for whatever it therein for them there being no blemish in it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There will be no disputes therein of their enemies, and there would happen to be for them in it what they would be loving. And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> took the Covenant upon the entirety of the Imams<sup>asws</sup> and their<sup>asws</sup> Shias with that. And rather, the greetings upon him<sup>saww</sup> is a reminder to the self of the Covenant and the renewal of it upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, perhaps He<sup>azwj</sup> the Majestic and Mighty might Hasten the peace for you all with the entirety of whatever is in it’.
en.sarwar: 39. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan who has said the following.
“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say, ‘O Lord, grant blessings up on Muhammad, Your chosen one, Your friend and Your selected one who manages Your affairs.”
